summary:
The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority over a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands. Myanmar called the ruling unfair, saying the decision was not unanimous and that it was unjustly accused. More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced, including 1.2 million in refugee camps in Bangladesh.

Russia launched one of its biggest air attacks yet on Ukraine, targeting Kyiv bridges days after Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge. The Kyiv mayor said the attacks damaged two bridges, and a day-long attack also damaged embassies. Two Russian cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone were reported to have crashed in Poland during the attacks, and Prime Minister Tusk called the incident an intentional provocation by Moscow. No one was hurt.

The leaders of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes in Shenzhen and issued a joint declaration towards peace. It covers UN reform, boosting oil supplies and protection of diplomatic immunity, but makes no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Trump called Putin his friend, and the three leaders denounced nuclear war.

headlines.title: Draft UN climate deal drops all mention of fossil fuels
headlines.summary: Co-host Australia unveiled a new draft agreement for the COP31 talks in Turkey that removes any mention of fossil fuels, drawing anger from campaign groups. The nearly 200 nations involved have until a set deadline to agree.

headlines.title: UK and EU agree reset deal, but tuition fees remain unresolved
headlines.summary: Downing Street said the UK and EU had agreed a reset deal at a Brussels summit, but the tuition fees EU students will pay in the UK remain unresolved. The EU said the deal would not take effect without a further agreement on those fees.

headlines.title: White House cyber chief Sean Cairncross leaves after tech outages
headlines.summary: Sean Cairncross is leaving his role as national cyber director after outages disrupted US air travel, banking and national security systems, though a person close to the White House said he was fired. Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, will serve in an acting capacity.

headlines.title: California investigates Nvidia over possible chip exports to China
headlines.summary: California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia to determine whether chip exports ended up in China and whether the company misled investors. State attorney general Rob Bonta said the matter raises bright red flags.
